description:
We are a team of enthusiastic students interested in science, technology, space exploration, and problem-solving. We are eager to learn new things, share ideas, and work together to develop creative solutions to real-world challenges.

We are looking for team members who are passionate, responsible, cooperative, and willing to contribute their skills and ideas. Everyone is welcome to join, regardless of experience!
summary: This project features an interactive 3D web application designed to make complex satellite ocean data accessible by tracking phytoplankton dynamics, chlorophyll-a concentration trends and global sea-level indicators. By allowing users to explore specific marine zones—specifically the Western Pacific and the North Sea, alongside predictive context and future recommendations, the platform transforms abstract environmental data into intuitive visual insights. This tool is crucial for raising public awareness about marine primary production and aquatic ecosystems, empowering students and researchers to better understand changing global ocean conditions.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

The project is an interactive 3D web application called Earth System. It works by rendering a fully interactive 3D globe using Three.js (WebGL) complete with atmospheric layers. Users can select specific marine regions—currently featuring the Western Pacific and the North Sea and click a "Focus region" button that smoothly animates the camera to rotate and zoom into those exact geographic coordinates. Once a region is selected, the application dynamically updates a multi-tabbed sidebar panel containing:

  • Interactive Data Charts: SVG-based line charts tracking chlorophyll-a concentration over time alongside a global sea level rise reference.
    • Three.js (v0.169.0) for 3D WebGL rendering, lighting, texture mapping, and sprite management.
    • Three.js OrbitControls for interactive mouse rotation, and zooming.
  • Graphics & UI: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) for precise line charts, HTML Canvas for dynamic 3D sprite labels, and custom CSS Flexbox/Grid for responsive dashboard styling.
  • Software/Environment: Standard web browser and code editor; texture maps and 3D assets loaded securely via high-performance CDNs. 5. How is your project creative? The project creatively bridges immersive graphics technology with scientific data visualization. Rather than presenting static charts on a flat webpage, it embeds analytics directly onto a living, breathing 3D digital twin of Earth. The programmatic camera animation (focusRegion slerp/lerp math) creates a cinematic transition when jumping from global orbit down to regional coordinates, making data exploration feel engaging, exploratory, and modern. 6. What factors did your team consider?
  • User Experience (UX) & Responsiveness: The team ensured the layout adapts smoothly between desktop monitors and smaller mobile screens by dynamically shifting panel sizes and globe offsets.
  • Scientific Honesty & Transparency: Rather than overclaiming, the interface explicitly notes the scope and limitations of the datasets (e.g., distinguishing global sea-level rise context from localized regional samples) and provides a clear roadmap of future recommendations.
  • Performance: Optimized WebGL rendering, texture loading states, and lightweight SVG charts ensure fast load times and smooth 60fps frame rates
